name: Majestic Genesis
oracle_text: Reveal the top X cards of your library, where X is the greatest mana value of a commander you own on the battlefield or in the command zone. You may put any number of permanent cards from among them onto the battlefield. Put the rest on the bottom of your library in a random order.
blocked_sentences: Reveal the top X cards of your library, where X is the greatest mana value of a commander you own on the battlefield or in the command zone.

needs.what: An `owner` key in the effect-side selector language (`SELECTOR_KEYS` / `matches` / `validate_selector` in src/automtg/engine/effects/selectors.py), taking the same player spec `controller` takes, and answered from `obj.owner` rather than `obj.controller`. It is what lets a pool be 'a commander you OWN on the battlefield', which is the only clause of this card that cannot be written. The rest of the sentence already exists: `extreme_value` reads a single greatest mana value off a pool, `union` assembles that pool from two zones, `zone: "command"` is a real zone and `player: "you"` already scopes it to the commanders you own there -- so this one key finishes the line, and it finishes every other 'a permanent/card you own' clause with it.
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `controller` is the closest thing and is the only ownership-shaped key `validate_selector` accepts -- `SELECTOR_KEYS` has no `owner`, so writing one is a load error, not a silent miss. `controller: "you"` is a different set in a game this engine can actually reach, because `gain_control` is implemented: it MISSES your own commander while an opponent controls it (the printed card still counts it, 903.3 -- a commander is defined by ownership) and it COUNTS an opponent's commander you have taken control of (the printed card does not). Either way X comes out wrong, and it comes out wrong silently. `player` cannot stand in: `validate_selector` deliberately refuses `player` on the battlefield because that zone list is shared, and it is right to -- `player` picks whose zone list to walk, which is exactly why it DOES say the command-zone half correctly. Nothing else in `selector_keys` reads ownership. The asymmetry is the tell: `cost_reduction_filter_keys` already has `owner`, and data/authoring/answers/visions_of_glory.json spells this identical printed clause -- 'where X is the greatest mana value of a commander you own on the battlefield or in the command zone' -- as `{"greatest_mana_value": {"is_commander": true, "owner": "you", "zone": ["battlefield", "command"]}}` in its flashback `mana_reduction`. The cost language can say it; the effect/value language has no equivalent, so the same sentence on two cards in the same deck would have to mean two different things.

notes: Everything after the first sentence is expressible and is deliberately not written as a partial answer. The whole card is one `look_at_top` in `spell_effects`: `amount` an `{"extreme_value": {"of": "mana_value", "pick": "greatest", "objects": {"union": [<commanders you own on the battlefield>, {"zone": "command", "player": "you", "is_commander": true}]}}}`, `objects` `{"count": "any", "any_types": ["Artifact", "Battle", "Creature", "Enchantment", "Land", "Planeswalker"]}`, `destination: "battlefield"` and `rest_to_bottom: true` -- which is Through the Forest Gate's shape plus the remainder key `op_look_at_top` documents against Florian's exact printed words, 'put the rest on the bottom of your library in a random order'. Only the first branch of the union is unsayable. Note for whoever measures this card once the key exists: build_sandbox gives player 0 no commander, so X evaluates to 0 (an empty pool is 0 by `extreme_value`'s own rule), nothing is revealed and nothing is put onto the battlefield -- the honest expectation in that position is `{"zone": "graveyard", "library_size": {"0": 40}, "battlefield_count": 32}`, and a sandbox commander would be needed to observe anything more.
